content_voiceover: This is a British Journal of Haematology paper on refining risk stratification in pediatric B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia by combining IKZF1plus status with Day 15 minimal residual disease positivity. IKZF1plus refers to IKZF1 deletion occurring together with deletions in other genes such as CDKN2A, CDKN2B, PAX5, or PAR1, in the absence of ERG deletion, and it is a well-established marker of poor prognosis. The five panels show Kaplan-Meier and cumulative incidence curves comparing wild-type IKZF1, shown in red, against IKZF1 deletion, shown in blue. Panel A shows five-year event-free survival, which is clearly worse for the deletion group. Panel B shows relapse-free survival, again worse with deletion. Panel C shows overall survival, also significantly worse with deletion, all with p values less than 0.0001. Panel D looks at cumulative incidence of isolated central nervous system relapse, which shows a trend toward more events in the deletion group but does not reach statistical significance. Panel E looks at cumulative incidence of any central nervous system relapse, including combined relapses, and this difference is statistically significant. The overall message is that IKZF1 deletion, especially when combined with Day 15 MRD positivity as IKZF1plus, identifies a group of patients who need intensified therapy because their risk of relapse and death is substantially higher.
keypoints: IKZF1plus combines IKZF1 deletion with CDKN2A, CDKN2B, PAX5, or PAR1 deletion, without ERG deletion
IKZF1 deletion is associated with significantly worse 5-year event-free survival, relapse-free survival, and overall survival, all p less than 0.0001
Isolated CNS relapse trend is higher with IKZF1 deletion but not statistically significant
Any CNS relapse, including combined relapses, is significantly higher with IKZF1 deletion
keypoint_voiceover: For boards, know that IKZF1plus, meaning IKZF1 deletion plus other gene deletions without ERG deletion, is a strong adverse prognostic marker in B-ALL. It predicts worse event-free survival, relapse-free survival, and overall survival. Combining it with Day 15 MRD positivity sharpens risk stratification and identifies patients who need therapy intensification.
